text:
noah: Heads up — onboarding got weird when I tried the new sample app after upgrading redwoodctl. I ran `redwoodctl auth login` via the GUI installer flow, it said login successful, but `redwoodctl localserve` returned 401s.

noah: Looking around I found the token under `~/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/default/token.json` on my Linux box, but the installer deposited a token at `/etc/redwood/profiles/default/token.json`.

noah: So two problems: installer is doing an OS-global path on linux (shouldn't for user installs), and CLI defaults to XDG user config.

tess: ouch. Which distro and did you use the system package?

noah: Ubuntu 22.04, used our .deb. I did a user install because it was easier for the sample app. The .deb postinst script writes to /etc/ by mistake when run with root uid even for user flows.

shaun: that's a packaging script bug — postinst is running unconditionally as root and writing global profiles. We should detect if user intended per-user install and write to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config.

packaging: ack, opened PKG-2048: "deb postinst must honor per-user install intent; avoid writing global profiles for user installs". Patch branch: packaging/deb-fix-profile-path.

noah: workaround for now was to copy the token to my XDG path and `export REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR="$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles"`. That fixed localserve immediately.

tess: another related note — I saw two token schema variants across installs: older token.json used `expires_at` (unix seconds) while new code expects `expiry` (RFC3339). When I copied a legacy token file localserve failed to parse it. Can CLI accept both formats?

shaun: yes, we should add a compatibility shim to parse `expires_at` and translate to `expiry` at load time, with a warning on first use. Also a migration command `redwoodctl profiles migrate --from=legacy` would be helpful.

packaging: adding to PKG-2048: compatibility shim and a migration UX. Also will add a small postinst migration step that does not overwrite user edits — it should only migrate files if target doesn't exist.

qa-bot: QA checklist attached to PKG-2048: test fresh deb install (user and system), upgrade path with legacy tokens, migration CLI, and ensure headless flows in CI don't get affected.

noah: small but important CI edge: `redwoodctl auth login --headless` printed the device code and then attempted to call `xdg-open` which fails inside non-GUI CI and returns an error exit code — our test runner flagged that as a failure. For headless we should only print the URL and succeed (no opener spawn).

shaun: agree. Add detection: if not isatty or if DISPLAY/XDG_SESSION_TYPE unset, skip opener spawn. Also add `--no-open` / `--browser=none` explicit flags.

packaging: logged PKG-2049: "headless login must not spawn opener in non-GUI environments; provide explicit flags".

ci-bot: Note: I detected failing CI job pipeline 3221 where e2e sample-app test flaked due to opener spawn; will rerun after patch.

tess: one more UX ask — when localserve can't read a profile because it's in /etc or ProgramData with restrictive perms, the error today is a generic 403. Can we make it actionable? e.g., "Cannot read profile at <path>. If this is a system install, run `redwoodctl auth login --profile=default` as the installing user or set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR to a readable path."

shaun: yep, will update CLI error messages to include path suggestions and the env var hint. Also log a checksum of the token file to help triage.

noah: thanks. I'll validate the deb canary once PKG-2048 lands. Happy to test migration and headless login behavior in our CI images.

packaging: thanks — will ping here when canary builds are available. Meanwhile, adding docs snippet to onboarding guide showing `REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR` and the one-liner migration copy: `mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles" && cp -R "/etc/redwood/profiles/"* "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/"`.

ci-bot: canary scheduled: packaging/deb-fix-profile-path -> canary-ubuntu at 2026-05-07T06:00Z

noah: perfect. Will test canary and report any anomalies. Thanks all!
